subject: LBM 2.0?
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Read the recent write-up of TRI's LBM study & was curious to understand how the team is thinking about further fine-tuning - so thought it'd be a good opportunity to introduce myself. 

I lead a Physical AI / Robotics team here at Encord, working with Woven (who I know you'll be very familiar with), Pickle Robot, Archetype AI & other leading teams - providing the platform to support the fine-tuning of Multimodal foundation models with strong support for video tracking & VLA annotations.

Curious to know if scaling training data pipelines is likely to be a priority as the team further improves its LBMs? 

Let me know if it makes sense to chat, happy to give some ideas based on how we're working with similar teams,

subject: Training data pipeline for perception model
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Mytra who was moving from simulation to real-world data collection to train their perception model. At the time they lacked a system to effectively index, auto-label and QA to keep up with the surging training data volume. I wonder if those are the challenges you've encountered at [COMPANY] Technologies? 

In case Encord is new to you - we help physical AI teams (e.g. Skydio, Zipline, Mytra, etc.) automate their annotation pipelines as they scale. Handful of customers in the space leverage our model-assisted workflow and our labelling editor's support across 2D (image & video) and 3D point cloud data, as a complement to Foxglove.

Keen to hear how you're thinking about your training data as you scale? I'm flexible Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to chat.

subject: Encord & [COMPANY]
text:
Hi [NAME],

Pretty cool to read up about the acquisition of Mirriad's - very impressive
to see the young AI company buying up the legacy player. We work
with Synthesia, Flawless, Captions and other content AI companies who
struggled with ensuring annotators actually label with care (rather than
rushing for incentives).

We've helped those teams navigate that balance ssing our data analytics
suite to identify the most valuable samples to label or review, and by
building QA workflows around HITL annotation - so high-impact samples get
high-quality labels, every time.

In case encord isn't familiar - we're a multimodal data curation and
annotation platform (Series B, $50m raised, 100+ FTEs).

Would love to set up a time to see if we can support you with any
challenges in your ML pipeline and introduce ourselves  - let me know if
you're free for a quick call and demo of our platform?

subject: Encord & Verdant
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congratulations on Verdant making THRIVE's Top 50 - looks like you're
building something really impactful in CV. We work with teams like Aigen
(robotics for de-weeding) who used to struggle with surfacing the right
edge cases for annotation - it was hurting their model performance. These
days, we mostly help them curate the right data and tie that directly into
their annotation workflows, which has made a big difference and streamlined
their ML pipelines as they scale into new use cases.

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord - we're a data development
platform focused on helping CV and multimodal teams build better models
(been around ~5 years, 70+ people, backed by top VCs).

Would you be up for a quick intro call to see if we could help in any way?
